card_summary: The National Retail Federation has built its own broadcast studio. This studio is equipped with the latest technology for live signal transport. The studio's infrastructure supports ST 2110 and AES67 for audio over IP, ensuring low latency and maintaining signal integrity. The use of 12G-SDI and JPEG XS enables high-quality video transport with frame-accuracy, crucial for live productions.

Technical Analysis: National Retail Federation Leverages JPEG XS for Low-Latency Live Signal Transport

The National Retail Federation has announced the construction of its own broadcast studio, incorporating the latest advancements in live signal transport technology, including JPEG XS compression. This development is significant, as it enables the organization to produce high-quality, low-latency live content for its members and stakeholders. The studio's infrastructure is built around the SMPTE ST 2110 standard, ensuring interoperability and flexibility in signal routing and processing.

Operational ROI

The adoption of JPEG XS compression in the National Retail Federation's broadcast studio is expected to yield significant operational savings, primarily through reduced transmission costs. By leveraging JPEG XS, the organization can achieve visually lossless compression at ratios of up to 10:1, resulting in lower bandwidth requirements for live signal transport. This, in turn, reduces the cost of transmitting high-quality live video signals over IP networks, making it an attractive solution for applications where latency and signal integrity are critical. The specific workflow step affected is the contribution feed, where JPEG XS enables the transport of high-quality live signals over existing network infrastructure, eliminating the need for costly fibre or satellite links.

In comparison to traditional uncompressed video transport methods, such as 12G-SDI, the use of JPEG XS compression offers a more efficient and cost-effective solution for live signal transport. The existing approach often requires dedicated fibre links or satellite transmissions, which can be expensive and prone to signal degradation. In contrast, JPEG XS compression enables the use of standard IP networks, simplifying signal routing and reducing the hardware rack footprint required for signal processing and transport.

Security & Integration

The integration of JPEG XS compression into the National Retail Federation's broadcast studio is designed to meet the stringent security and compliance requirements of the broadcast industry. The studio's infrastructure is built around the SMPTE ST 2110 standard, which provides a framework for secure and interoperable live signal transport over IP networks. Additionally, the use of AES67 audio over IP and NMOS IS-04 device registration and connection management ensures seamless integration with existing broadcast equipment and systems. The studio's signal routing and processing infrastructure is also designed to meet the requirements of the RIST specification for reliable internet stream transport, ensuring secure and reliable signal transport over IP networks.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Deployment: The deployment of JPEG XS compression in the National Retail Federation's broadcast studio requires a minimum network bandwidth of 1 GbE, as well as compatible hardware and software components, such as JPEG XS-enabled encoders and decoders.
  • Compatibility: The studio's infrastructure is designed to be compliant with the SMPTE ST 2110-20 standard for uncompressed video over IP, as well as the NMOS IS-04 specification for device registration and connection management.
  • What to Watch: The upcoming update to the SMPTE ST 2110 standard, which is expected to include new specifications for compressed video over IP, is an important development that engineers should track, as it may impact the design and deployment of future live signal transport systems.

The National Retail Federation's adoption of JPEG XS compression for live signal transport marks an important milestone in the broadcast industry's transition to IP-based infrastructures. As the industry continues to evolve, engineering teams should focus on developing a deep understanding of the technical requirements and implications of IP-based live signal transport, including the use of JPEG XS compression and other related technologies.

Analysis: The National Retail Federation's in-house broadcast studio will likely utilize ST 2110 for IP-based video transport, enabling efficient signal routing and processing within the facility.
